---
title: Use your own API keys
description: Use Claude, GPT, Grok and Gemini models with your own Anthropic, OpenAI, xAI or Google API key in chat, the Advisor and Design, next to your GitHub Copilot models.
---

With your own API keys, Fabricator's model pickers also offer models from other providers,
next to the models in your GitHub Copilot plan:

| Provider | Models | Billed to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Anthropic** | Claude models | Your Anthropic account |
| **OpenAI** | GPT models | Your OpenAI account |
| **xAI** | Grok models | Your xAI account |
| **Google** | Gemini and Gemma models | The Google Cloud project your key belongs to |

You still sign in to GitHub Copilot. Copilot runs the conversation on your computer: it
reads and edits your project the same way, and it calls the provider with your key whenever
you choose one of its models.

## Add a key

1. Open **Model providers** in **Accounts**: in a model picker, select **Manage API keys…** at
   the bottom, or **Add models with your API keys…** in its list of models. You can also
   select **Manage API keys** in **Settings**.
2. Find the provider and select **Add key**.
3. Paste your key into the box. To create one, select **Get a key**, which opens the
   provider's key page in your browser.
4. Select **Save key**.

Fabricator checks the key with the provider before it keeps it. If the provider turns it
down, you see a message such as "OpenAI didn't accept this key. Check that you copied all of
it." and nothing is saved.

![Model providers in Accounts: an Anthropic key saved, with Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 turned on for the model pickers, and an OpenAI key being added](/screenshots/model-providers.webp)

When the key works, the card shows **API key** and where it's kept, such as "Saved in
Windows Credential Manager". On macOS, keys are kept in your Keychain.

## Choose which models the pickers show

Under **In the model pickers**, each card lists the provider's models that your key can use,
with each model's context window, and `images` when it can read images. The models marked
**Recommended** are turned on when you add a key. A model marked **Retiring** is one the
provider is phasing out.

- Turn a model on or off with its checkbox. The pickers update right away.
- Select **Show all** to see every model your key can use.
- Select **Check again** to check the saved key with the provider and update its list of
  models.

## Pick one of your models

1. In the chat composer, open the model pill.
2. Turn off **Auto**, then select **Model**.
3. Choose a model under **Your API keys**. The provider's name is next to each one.

![The model picker with Auto off, the model list open, Copilot's models with their makers' logos, and the models on the user's own Anthropic and OpenAI keys under Your API keys](/screenshots/model-picker.webp)

The pill shows a key next to a model that runs on your own key. To change keys or models,
select **Manage API keys…** at the bottom of the picker.

The same picker is in the **Advisor** bar and the Design bar.
In Design, **Auto** means Fabricator picks a fast Copilot model for **Options** and
**Polish**; it never picks a model on your own key by itself. See
[Choose a model and reasoning effort](/docs/build/chat#choose-a-model-and-reasoning-effort).

You can switch models at any time, also in the middle of a conversation. The next message
uses the model you chose.

## Models that can't read images

Some models can't read images. While one of them is selected, **Image** in the composer's
**+** menu says that the model can't read images. If you already attached images, Fabricator
holds the message until you remove them or choose a model that can read images.

## Replace or remove a key

- To use a different key, select **Replace**, paste the new key, and select **Replace key**.
  Fabricator keeps the old key if the provider doesn't accept the new one.
- To remove a key, select **Remove**, then select **Remove** again to confirm. Its models
  leave the pickers. A chat, Advisor or Design set to one of them asks you to choose another
  model.

## Plans and limits

The provider bills your account for what its models use, and its plan sets your limits.
Fabricator's requests are large: each one carries Fabricator's instructions, tools and parts
of your app.

- Some plans cap the tokens a key can use a minute, so a smaller plan may turn these
  requests down. If that happens, Fabricator says, for example, "This request is bigger than
  your OpenAI plan allows per minute." Upgrade your plan with the provider, or choose
  another model.
- Google's free tier allows only a few requests a minute and a day. If Fabricator says
  "Google is limiting how often your key can be used", wait and try again, or turn on
  billing for your key's Google Cloud project.

For other errors from a provider, see
[A model on your own API key shows an error](/docs/troubleshooting/chat#a-model-on-your-own-api-key-shows-an-error).

## Your keys and privacy

- Fabricator keeps your keys in Windows Credential Manager, or in your Keychain on macOS.
  They never go into Fabricator's settings, logs or diagnostics, and Fabricator never shows
  a saved key.
- When you use one of your models, Copilot on your computer sends your request and the
  project context it needs straight to the provider, under the provider's terms for your
  account.
- Requests to OpenAI, xAI and Google pass through a relay on your computer that adapts them
  to what each provider's API accepts: for example, it leaves out a reasoning effort a model
  doesn't take. Nothing leaves your computer through it except the request to that provider.
  While Fabricator runs, the relay keeps the signatures Gemini adds to its tool calls in
  memory, to send them back with the conversation.

See [Privacy](/docs/reference/privacy#your-own-api-keys).
